title: Compact quant hypothesis notes — May 05 2027
content:
Context: quick capture from this week's bench / sync focused on compact (4-bit-ish) quant hypotheses and practical onboarding for two customer models (gpt-neox-20B-like variant and a bloated instruction-tuned 7B). Rough, intentionally terse — meant as a running lab notebook for the week and handoff notes for next sprint.

Attendees: Lena Chen (note), Marco Ruiz, Priya Varma, Oskar Bjorn, Maya Singh, (brief drop-ins from infra: Daniel Foster).

Agenda:
- Summaries from each experiment cluster (quant profiles, KV cache interactions, eval regressions)
- Weird latency bump on small-batch streaming after qat pass
- Model onboarding checklist gotchas (tokenizer, EOS handling, special tokens)
- Next steps + tickets to open/triage

High-level takeaways (TL;DR):
- 4-bit symmetric per-channel + block size 64 (our compact config "c4s64") is promising on throughput (2.4x speedup CPU-hosted quant workloads) with small average PPL degradation (~1.6%) on short-context instruction set. But failure modes: long-context instruction summaries degrade more (PPL delta ~6–9%) on safety-sensitive prompts.
- KV-cache interacts poorly with quantized key/value packing when sequence > 2048 tokens: alignment bug suspected in packing/offset math, causing occasional token repetition.
- Canary onboarding of the 7B instr-tuned model surfaced tokenizer mismatch: byte-level vs sentencepiece fallback causes off-by-one EOS in streaming. Fix is in PR (see linked PR) but must be validated across serving-runtime streaming path.

Experiment cluster A — quant profiles (compact c4s64 vs baseline fp16):
- Models: internal-gpt-neox-20B-mini (dev), cust-7B-instr (customer test).
- Configs tried: c4s64 (per-channel symmetric, block=64), c4s32 (block=32), q8-ptq (8-bit PTQ baseline), fq2 (fake 2-bit probe).
- Metrics collected: PPL on instr-dev-set-200 (short instrs), MMLU-subset-10, latency p50/p95 for gen length 64 and 512, GPU memory usage, throughput (tokens/s).

Representative results (dev numbers):
- gpt-neox-20B-mini:
  - fp16 baseline: PPL=10.2; p50 latency(64)=92ms; throughput=510 tokens/s
  - c4s64: PPL=10.4 (+1.9%); p50(64)=42ms (-54%); throughput=1230 tokens/s (+2.4x)
  - c4s32: PPL=10.6 (+3.9%); p50(64)=39ms; throughput=1300 tokens/s (slight gain but higher PPL)
  - q8-ptq: PPL=10.3; p50(64)=58ms; throughput=870 tokens/s
- cust-7B-instr:
  - fp16 baseline: PPL=5.8; c4s64: PPL=6.2 (+6.9%) on long-summary prompts (gen=512). Short prompts less affected.

Notes/observations:
- The PPL reg is not uniform: sampling-based eval (top-k) shows larger divergence than greedy eval, implying quant noise amplifies non-linear decoding.
- Instruction compliance metrics (manual grade on 50 sampled prompts) shows fewer hallucinations with c4s64 on factual queries, but more hallucinations on multi-step reasoning (likely reduced numeric precision hurting chain-of-thought token-level fidelity).
- c4s64 looks like the best throughput/quality sweet spot for many production workloads, but must be gated for long-context pipelines and LLM-based summarization customers.

Experiment cluster B — KV cache & packing investigations:
- Symptom: intermittent token repeat loop after ~2500 tokens in long streaming sessions (repro rate ~15% in stress harness).
- Hypothesis: packing/align logic when storing KV shards into shared buffer fails to advance offset properly when multiple small requests (micro-batches) are interleaved + quantized key/value size rounding introduces alignment mismatches.
- Quick repro steps used: stress_stream_test.sh --model gpt-neox-20B-mini --seq 4096 --micro-batch 1 --quant=c4s64 (script in linked PR).
- Immediate workaround: force micro-batch >=4 or disable packed-KV dedup on sessions flagged >2048 tokens. This reduces repro rate to near 0 but increases memory.
- Action: Oskar to open JIRA-ML-2183 task to re-check buffer_offset arithmetic and add fuzz tests for odd-length KV writes.

Model onboarding notes (cust-7B-instr):
- Tokenizer: customer's export used a legacy byte-level tokenizer; our runtime expects sentencepiece by default. Streaming's EOS fallback path appended a stray 0x00, causing the model to consider an early stop token in a small fraction of cases.
- Fix: add tokenizer compatibility shim (PR linked). Validate by running token-level diff on 10k sample tokens. Priya to own validation.
- Special tokens: <INSTRUCT_START> / <INSTRUCT_END> were missing from model config json. We had to patch config and re-index embeddings table mapping. That caused one training artifact (unused token embedding) to be referenced; safe to ignore but document in onboarding checklist.

Evals & safety checks:
- Quick eval sets used: instr-dev-set-200 (internal), mmlu-mini-10, hallucination-probe-30.
- For c4s64: pass rate (instruction compliance) on instr-dev-set-200 = 88% (baseline fp16 = 91%). MMLU-mini diff within margin for math/science but lower on long multi-hop questions.
- Safety probe: c4s64 introduced 2 regression cases for toxic-output-less prompting; need to triage whether quantization introduced numerical instabilities in logit gaps. Add to regression watchlist.

Perf anomaly — streaming latency bump:
- Symptom: occasionally p95 spikes by ~300ms for gen length 64 sequences when running QAT'd models. Observed on both NVMe-backed and tmpfs hosts but more pronounced on tmpfs (weird).
- Initial trace: increased time in exec_kernel_shuffle step; suspect kernel selection fallback for short sequences hitting a slower code path when quant params present. Marco to instrument kernel selection path and add counter metrics. PR #1847 contains an instrumentation patch.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is c4s64 safe for batches with mixed sequence lengths? We saw throughput cliffs and higher variance. Need synthetic benchmark mixing short & long contexts.
- Does quant noise change tokenization boundaries for byte-level tokenizers more than sentencepiece? Priya suspects yes.
- What's the minimal guardrail for rollout? Candidate gating: (1) perf SLOs met p95<500ms for 64 tokens; (2) instruction compliance >=89%; (3) KV-cache no repro at 4096 tokens stress.

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Oskar: JIRA-ML-2183 — add fuzz tests + fix offset math (ETA 2d).
- Marco: finish kernel-selection instrumentation and run p95 stratified by quant config (ETA 3d). Link in PR #1847 for review.
- Priya: tokenizer compatibility validation 10k sample token diff & run streaming smoke tests for cust-7B-instr (ETA 2d).
- Lena: create canary checklist for c4s64 rollout and draft runbook for quick rollback if hallucination regressions observed (ETA 1d).
- Maya: expand eval set (add 100 long-context summarization prompts), run overnight suite with c4s64 and q8-ptq to collect longer-context PPL/time series (ETA overnight).

Notes to self / messy thoughts:
- Consider hybrid approach: use c4s64 for short-context inference pods (chat + search) and fallback q8-ptq for long-context summarization pods; runtime can auto-route by route-config. Needs per-route model variant mapping in rollout UI.
- Long-term: probe learned quantization aware finetuning (QAT) with 1 epoch on distillation dataset to recover chain-of-thought fidelity — run small trial on 7B instr-tuned model.

Links / quick refs (in doc):
- Perf instrumentation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1847
- KV fuzz starter harness: repo://applied-ml/kv-fuzz (internal)
- Jira: JIRA-ML-2183 (KV packing offset bug)
- Confluence: quantization-playbook (living doc)


End of notes. Will update after Oskar/Marco checkins and overnight evals.

Quick footer: if anyone reading wants a copy of the raw bench CSVs, ping me (Lena) — they're large (~120MB) but I can drop a trimmed sample in the shared bench folder.
